articles.raw_meta: This year’s El Niño weather pattern is to blame, according to scientists
articles.jina_text:
The remaining months of the Atlantic hurricane season could be relatively quiet, a new federal prediction shows - but not everywhere is as lucky. 
There are between 2 and 6 hurricanes, 0 and 2 major hurricanes, and 7 to 13 named storms expected in the Atlantic for the rest of the year, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration said on Thursday.
That’s a slight reduction from an initial forecast issued in May and lower than the average season, though it only takes one major storm to threaten lives.





Precipitation below average along the eastern and southern shores is tied to an El Niño Climate pattern, NOAA said.
This pattern is also what’s responsible for an above-average hurricane year in the Pacific season, which sees storms hit Hawaii and along the West Coast.






open image in gallery
This image of Tropical Storm Bertha moving along the Gulf Coast was captured by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s GOES East satellite last month. NOAA just issued an updated outlook for the Atlantic season showing more below-normal activity in the basin - but a different story elsewhere (NOAA Satellites)





open image in gallery
Kids play in the floodwaters from Tropical Storm Bertha in New Orleans, Louisiana, last month. The storm was one of two named storms in the Atlantic this year (AP)





open image in gallery
Children play near breaking waves from Tropical Storm Bertha in New Orleans, Louisiana, last month. There have been no hurricanes in the Atlantic yet (AP)
Plus, this year’s El Niño is particularly strong - it’s being called a “super” or “Godzilla” El Niño, boosted by excess heat stored in Earth’s oceans.


Hurricanes need warm ocean temperatures to form, and record temperatures in the Atlantic have supercharged some of the biggest hurricanes in recent years.
“When El Niño emerges, it usually becomes the dominant factor in total hurricane season activity, and this El Niño continues to get stronger every month,” Matt Rosencrans, lead hurricane season forecaster with NOAA’s National Weather Service, explained in a statement.





open image in gallery
Brad Reinhart, Senior Hurricane Specialist, works on tracking Tropical Storm Arthur at the National Hurricane Center in June in Miami, Florida. NOAA says El Nino has been behind below-normal Atlantic hurricane activity (Getty Images)
Other mechanisms that determine the number and intensity of tropical storms in the Atlantic play a smaller role, he noted.



That’s why the outlook for the Eastern Pacific hurricane season is unchanged, with 15-22 named storms and the Central Pacific basin could see between 5-13 named storms.





So far, there have been seven named storms in the Eastern Pacific, including two that became hurricanes named Fausto and Genevieve.

articles.jina_text:
Two councillors have come under fire in west London after being accused of climate change denial amid a drought in London.




In a Facebook comment, Councillor Darshan Nagi, the Conservative councillor for Hounslow East, described climate change as a “natural process.” He added: “It started from ice age and haz been happening since upto now and it will carry on NOTHING WILL STOP IT.”








“ALL THESE ORGANISATIONS WHO ARE HYPING UP CLIMATE CHANGE AND TAKING MONEY IN DIFFERENT TAXES AND [CHARGES] AND PAYING THEMSELVES HIGH WAGEZ AND GIVING FUNDING TO MULTINATIONAL COMPANIES TO PREVENT [CLIMATE] CHANGE. I WOULD CALM THEM………….”




Cllr Nagi’s comment was made below a post on Brentford Today reporting on the Leader of Hounslow Reform, Cllr Tony Brown, reposting tweets which say “climate emergency is a big hoax.”




Cllr Jack Emsley, Leader of the Hounslow Conservative Group, told the Local Democracy Reporting Service [LDRS] that this is not the view of the wider group, nor was it policy. 


Councillor Tony Brown, Hounslow Reform Leader
Hounslow Council




In a written statement, Cllr Nagi said that his comment was clumsy, and rejects the assertion that he said climate change is not real.













He said: “The comment on Facebook doesn’t represent the view of the party or the Conservative Group. I was trying to convey that climate change is a big process that won’t be stopped by one country alone pursuing net zero.




“I appreciate my comment was quite clumsy, but at no point have I said climate change isn’t real – rather, the current policies that the government claims are supposed to tackle climate change are in fact about raising revenue as opposed to mitigating the impact of our changing climate.”









When approached by the LDRS about his reposts on X which claim that climate change is a hoax and implied scientists are “hiding something from you”, Cllr Brown said his view on the matter is “quite nuanced.” He added: “The fact that I have liked a tweet does NOT make it my definitive position on the subject.




“What I do believe is that prosperity through growth makes any society much more effective in being able to mitigate climate change. And it is in that context that net zero measures having given us the highest industrial electricity prices in the world is doubly unfortunate.

Trump orders new 15% tariff on key material for solar panels and microchips


Move to raise levy on goods made with polysilicon aims to protect domestic US supply chains from China, the major producer




Donald Trump has ordered a new 15% tariff on imported products made of polysilicon, an important ingredient in microchip manufacturing that is primarily produced by China.
The new tariff, which will take effect on 4 December, is aimed at supporting US chip and solar panel supply chains to compete with Beijing on artificial intelligence and energy.

The executive order signed by the president on Thursday evening said: “The plan of action in ⁠this proclamation will, among other things, help ensure the commercial viability of United States production of polysilicon and its derivatives that is necessary to meet United States economic and national security requirements.”
Polysilicon, an ultra-pure form of silicon, is an important ingredient in making the semiconductors vital for AI processing power, datacentres and solar power generation.
US solar factories have long accused Chinese ‌rivals of dumping cheaper panels on the ‌market, which they say have been enabled by excessive government subsidies and by moving manufacturing to other countries to dodge US tariffs.
China’s foreign affairs ministry hit back at the latest measures, accusing the US of “overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing state power to go after Chinese businesses”.


View image in fullscreen
Solar panels advance toward final testing at a First Solar manufacturing facility in Perrysburg, Ohio, US. Photograph: Emily Elconin/Bloomberg via Getty Images
“Protectionism will not make the US more competitive,” the spokesperson Lin Jian said, arguing that the move “seriously disrupts normal trade and economic exchanges between Chinese and US businesses, and is not in the interest of US businesses and consumers or anyone else for that matter”.


“China will continue firmly protecting our businesses’ legitimate and lawful rights and interests,” Lin added.
The US has two main polysilicon factories, including Hemlock Semiconductor, which operates ‌a plant in Michigan and is a joint venture between the US tech company Corning and Japan’s Shin-Etsu Handotai. The Munich-based Wacker Chemie runs a factory in Tennessee.
A spokesperson for Corning said the new tariff encouraged “continued investment in US capacity and supports long-term US competitiveness”, while Wacker said it appreciated the administration’s engagement “given the ramifications for semiconductor supply chain resilience, advanced computing infrastructure, and broader US defence and security interests”.
